stemBlocks.value: An incomplete Venn diagram shows a class of 28 students, where U is all students, F is those who play football and T is those who play tennis. 12 students play tennis, 15 play football, 8 play neither, and x play BOTH. Complete the diagram in terms of x and find the value of x, and hence the number who play football only and tennis only. (The workbook prints the stem and diagram here; the lettered parts continue beyond this extract.)
Think first: The 15 footballers and 12 tennis players overlap, so you cannot simply add them; label the football-only and tennis-only regions first.

contentBlocks.value: 15 play football in total, x of them also play tennis
12 play tennis in total, x of them also play football

solutionSteps.instruction: Add all four regions and set the sum to 28.

strategyBlocks.value: Write football only as 15 - x and tennis only as 12 - x, add all four regions including the 8 who play neither, set the sum to 28 and solve.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: x = 7 students play both sports; 8 play football only, 5 play tennis only, and 8 play neither, giving 28 in all.

whyThisWorks.value: The figures 15 and 12 are totals for the whole circles, so each already contains the x students in the overlap. Subtracting x gives the part of each circle that belongs to that sport alone, and only then do the regions add without double counting. The 8 who play neither sit outside both circles but still inside U, so they must be included in the total.

examTip.value: Fill a Venn diagram from the middle outwards. The intersection first, then the only regions, then the outside, and every count stays honest.
